title: Akhlaq of Artificial Intelligence, Information Security, and Responsible Digital Citizenship
summary: Entering university/work = higher digital responsibility: (1) Akhlaq of AI: Do not cheat with ChatGPT in assignments/research — use it as a thinking tool, not a substitute for effort. Cite the source, verify the information. (2) Information security: Strong/unique passwords, password manager, two-factor authentication (2FA) on all important accounts, device encryption, backups. (3) Privacy of others: Do not share others' photos/information without permission, respect GDPR/local protection systems. (4) Citizenship: Report harmful content, support victims of bullying, use technology for good. A digital citizen = an ethical professional.
try_this: This week: Enable 2FA on your top 5 accounts, install a password manager (Bitwarden/1Password), review app permissions on your phone.
reflection_prompts: Which accounts have you enabled 2FA on?
What new security habit will you start?

review_defects.why: The Arabic uses the modern secular term 'أخلاقيات' (ethics), not the Islamic term 'أخلاق' (akhlaq). Transliterating it as 'Akhlaq' imposes a religious connotation absent in the source, and the transliteration corresponds to a different Arabic word.
